summary: Kavita Singh (1964–2023) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College, MS University of Baroda, and Panjab University/University of the Punjab, and held posts at Marg Publications, College of Art, Delhi, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Kazi Dawa Samdup (1868–1922) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Bhutia Boarding School under Ugyen Gyatso and Tshampa Norbu. He later served as headmaster of Bhutia Boarding School (~1906–1919) and lectured at the University of Calcutta (1920).

Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyushu University (~1948–1992). He held academic positions at the University of Miyazaki (~1957–1968) and Seijo University (~1968–1995).

Kazuaki Komine (born 1947) is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who completed his degrees at Waseda University. He taught at Waseda Jitsugyo High School, Tokushima University, the National Institute of Japanese Literature, and Rikkyo University (1995–2013).

Kazuaki Tanahashi (born 1933) is an active scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Soichi Nakamura (~1950–1960). He was a scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center (1977–1984) and a fellow at the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After completing doctoral coursework at Kyoto University, he served on the faculty at Shuchiin University, where he is attested from 1982 to 2013.

Kazuharu Mizuno (born 1958) is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at Nagoya University, Hokkaido University, and Tokyo Metropolitan University. He served as a professor of geography at Kyoto University (~2009–2024).

Kazuhiko Atsumi (1928–2019) worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1954) and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1989) and Suzuka University of Medical Science (~1991–2000).

Kazuhiko Yoshida (born 1955) works in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Sophia, Kyoto, Osaka, and Cornell universities under Jay Jasanoff and Teizo Iyanaga, holding posts at Nagoya City Women's College, Kyoto University, and Nagoya City University.
Kazuhiro Kaneiwa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts at Bukkyo University, attested in 2001 and 2013.

Kazuhiro Kawasaki (born 1974) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies at Koyasan University, where he held positions as a researcher (attested 2005) and special appointed professor (attested 2026).
Kazuhiro Yamamoto is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Silpakorn University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya.
Kazumi Yoshizaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Toyo University and held a post at the National Museum of Ethnology (attested 2001).

Kazunobu Matsuda (born 1955) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Shiro Matsumoto, and held posts at Otani University, Bukkyo University (attested 1995–2024), and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Kazuo Enoki (1913–1989) was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1933–1936), later serving as an assistant professor there (~1948–1955) and holding a post at Toyo Bunko (~1957–1985).

Kazuo Hyodo (born 1948) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe, later serving as an assistant professor at Otani University (~1983–2014).

Kazuo Kano (born 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned degrees at Kyoto University and the University of Hamburg, holding posts at Hamburg, Kyoto University, Koyasan University, and Komazawa University.

Kazuo Matsumura (born 1953) works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Hitotsubashi University (~1972–1976) and held positions at Tenri University (~1986–1997) and Wako University (~2004–2019).

Kazuo Okabe (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, later holding posts at the Institute for Zen Studies and Komazawa University (1973–2006).

Kazuo Osumi (born 1933) is a scholar of Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and held posts at Hokkaido University (1964) and Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).
